content:
Any cyclist who finishes ahead of Vasya overall must have been faster than Vasya in at least one stage.

There are \(15\) stages, and in each stage exactly \(6\) cyclists are faster than Vasya. Thus there are only

\[
15\cdot 6 = 90
\]

stage-slots in which a cyclist can be faster than Vasya. Hence at most \(90\) distinct cyclists can have a total time less than Vasya’s total time.

So Vasya can be beaten by at most \(90\) cyclists, meaning his lowest possible position is \(91\).

This is achievable by assigning the \(90\) faster stage-slots to \(90\) distinct cyclists, one fast stage each, with a large enough advantage in that stage to outweigh small losses in the other \(14\) stages.

\[
\boxed{91}
\]
